The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph.
